_about: Teaching text for the cardinal-web help drawer. Written for this project (CC0). Module descriptions and manual links come from the engine; everything here is ours and fills the gap Rack leaves (module authors rarely describe knobs and jacks in code). Keys: modules['Plugin/Model'] = { about, try, params{name or #id: text}, inputs{...}, outputs{...}, names{params|inputs|outputs: {id: name}} }. Patterns apply to repeated knobs (Mod 1 to X, Step 12...) on any module.
conventions: Voltages: audio swings about ±5 V. Control voltage (CV) is usually 0 to 10 V, or ±5 V when bipolar. A gate is 10 V while something is on, 0 V when off; a trigger is a very short gate. Pitch follows 1 V per octave: +1 V doubles the frequency, 1/12 V is one semitone.

SurgeXTRack.note: Surge XT modules have four modulation inputs and a depth knob for every modulatable control. Those depth knobs are grouped below; the main controls come first.

MockbaModular.note: Mockba's tiny 2 HP modules leave most knobs unnamed in code; the names shown here are ours, taken from the source.

patterns.text: How far this modulation input moves the control it names. Centre is off; negative values invert the modulation.
Depth for one modulation input on one control. Centre is off.
One of the 64 step buttons. In sequence mode it turns the gate at that step on or off; in song mode it picks which sequence plays in that phrase.
When this step is reached, fire the trigger output.
The voltage this step sends while the sequencer sits on it. Turn it to set the note (1/12 V per semitone) or any other value you want stepped.
Chooses the rhythm pattern a step uses when its gate is on: full, half, triplets and so on.
One MIDI controller number mapped to a jack. Set which CC each cell listens to in the module's own panel; here the jack simply carries that controller as 0 to 10 V.
A gate for one MIDI note, 10 V while the key is held.
One voice of a polyphonic cable, as a plain mono signal.
One voice of one of the two polyphonic banks.
One of the switched signals.
How much of this input reaches the output, so the module works as a selector, a crossfader or a small mixer.
The base value for this target; the four modulators are added on top at the depths set below.
Target value plus modulation, as CV.
Whether this step fires the Trigger output when the sequencer reaches it. Off makes a rest.
Silence this source.
Hear only this source (and any other soloed one).
A leftover slot in the module's code; it does nothing.
A modulation signal (LFO, envelope, CV). How much it moves each control is set by the matching depth knobs.
Audio into this stereo channel. Patch Left alone for a mono source.
CV that takes over the knob of the same name on the Clocked module to its left.
Step entry by CV: writes the Gate input's state into the current step and moves on.

Fundamental/VCO.about: A voltage controlled oscillator: the sound source. It produces four waveforms at once from one pitch. Patch the Pitch jack from a sequencer or keyboard, take one waveform out to a filter or VCA.
Fundamental/VCO.try: With the arpeggio running, move a cable from the Sawtooth output to the Square output and listen to the tone change. Then sweep Pulse width while Square is playing.

params.Frequency: Base pitch, in semitones away from middle C (C4, 261.6 Hz). The Pitch jack adds to this at 1 V per octave, so leave it near 0 and let the sequencer set the notes.
params.Sync mode: What happens when the Sync input fires. Hard restarts the wave each time, giving the classic ripping sync tone; Soft only flips its direction.
params.Frequency modulation: How much the FM input shifts the pitch. Centre is off. Small amounts from an LFO give vibrato; large amounts from another oscillator give clangorous FM timbres.
params.Pulse width: Shape of the Square wave only: 50 % is a true square, towards 1 % or 99 % it becomes a thin, nasal pulse.
params.Pulse width modulation: How much the PWM input moves Pulse width. A slow LFO here is the classic chorusing pulse sound.
params.FM mode: 1V/octave: FM shifts pitch exponentially, so the note stays in tune relative to other voices. Linear: FM adds frequency in Hz, the mode used for bell-like through-zero FM.

inputs.1V/octave pitch: The note. Each volt doubles the frequency. Comes from a sequencer CV out, a quantizer, or a MIDI pitch out.
inputs.Frequency modulation: A signal that wobbles the pitch, scaled by the Frequency modulation knob. LFO for vibrato, audio for FM synthesis.
inputs.Sync: A rising edge restarts the wave. Patch another oscillator's Square here and tune this one above it.
inputs.Pulse width modulation: Moves Pulse width, scaled by the Pulse width modulation knob.

outputs.Sine: The purest tone, one harmonic. Smooth and quiet; good for sub bass and FM.
outputs.Triangle: Soft, flute-like; a few odd harmonics.
outputs.Sawtooth: Bright and full, every harmonic. The go-to wave for a filter to work on.
outputs.Square: Hollow, clarinet-like; odd harmonics only, and the only wave Pulse width changes.

Fundamental/VCF.about: A voltage controlled filter. It removes frequencies above (Lowpass) or below (Highpass) the cutoff, and can ring at the cutoff with resonance. Filters are where subtractive synthesis gets its character.
Fundamental/VCF.try: Patch VCO Sawtooth into Audio, Lowpass into the VCA's channel input, then sweep Cutoff frequency slowly. Add Resonance and sweep again.

params.Cutoff frequency: Where the filter starts cutting. In Lowpass everything above it is darkened; in Highpass everything below. The Frequency input adds to this at 1 V per octave.
params.Resonance: Emphasises frequencies right at the cutoff. Low gives a gentle tone shaper; high rings and whistles, and near maximum it self-oscillates into a sine tone.
params.Cutoff frequency CV: How much the Frequency input moves the cutoff. Centre is off, negative inverts. Patch an envelope into Frequency and raise this for the classic opening-and-closing sweep.
params.Drive: Gain into the filter. Pushing it adds saturation and grit before filtering.

inputs.Frequency: CV that moves the cutoff, through the Cutoff frequency CV knob. Envelopes, LFOs, or the pitch CV itself so the filter tracks the notes.
inputs.Resonance: CV for resonance, through its depth knob.
inputs.Drive: CV for drive, through its depth knob.
inputs.Audio: The sound to filter. Usually an oscillator or a mix of them.

outputs.Lowpass filter: Highs removed above the cutoff: warm, round, the usual synth filter sound.
outputs.Highpass filter: Lows removed below the cutoff: thin, bright. Both outputs run at once.

Fundamental/VCA-1.about: A voltage controlled amplifier: a volume knob that a voltage can turn. With an envelope on CV it shapes each note; with an LFO it makes tremolo. No note has a shape without a VCA.
Fundamental/VCA-1.try: Pull the cable out of CV and the sound stays on constantly at Level. Put it back and the envelope opens and closes it per note.

params.Level: Maximum gain. With nothing in CV, the signal passes at this level; with a CV patched, the CV scales from 0 up to this.
params.Response mode: Linear: gain follows the CV directly. Exponential: the same CV gives a curve that feels more natural for volume, quieter for longer then swelling.

inputs.CV: 0 to 10 V controls the gain, 10 V being full Level. Envelopes and LFOs go here.
inputs.Channel: The signal being controlled: audio from an oscillator or filter, or a CV you want to scale.

outputs.Channel: Input times gain. Send it to the Audio module or a mixer.

Fundamental/LFO.about: A low frequency oscillator: the same waveforms as a VCO, but running from one cycle every few minutes up to a few hundred hertz, used as a control voltage rather than heard. It is how a patch moves on its own.
Fundamental/LFO.try: Patch Triangle into the VCF Frequency input and raise the filter's Cutoff frequency CV knob. Slow the LFO Frequency down to hear the sweep.

params.Offset: Bipolar: the output swings ±5 V around zero. Unipolar: 0 to 10 V, which suits VCA and level inputs.
params.Invert: Flips the waveform upside down, so a rising ramp becomes a falling one.
params.Frequency: Speed, in cycles per second. 2 Hz is a fast wobble; 0.1 Hz is a ten second sweep. With a Clock patched in, this knob becomes an octave multiplier or divider of the clock.
params.Frequency modulation: Depth of the FM input: lets another CV speed the LFO up and down.
params.Pulse width: Shape of the Square output: how long it stays high in each cycle.

inputs.Frequency modulation: CV that changes the speed, through its depth knob.
inputs.Reset: A trigger restarts the cycle from the beginning, so the LFO lines up with the beat.
inputs.Pulse width modulation: CV for Pulse width, through its depth knob.
inputs.Clock: Patch a clock and the LFO locks its rate to it; the Frequency knob then multiplies or divides.

outputs.Triangle: Smooth, linear up then down; the usual choice for filter sweeps and vibrato.
outputs.Sawtooth: Ramps up then snaps back; rhythmic swells.
outputs.Square: On/off; works as a slow gate or clock as well as a CV.

Fundamental/ADSR.about: An envelope generator. When a gate arrives it rises (Attack), falls to a hold level (Decay to Sustain), and when the gate ends it fades out (Release). The output is 0 to 10 V, made to drive a VCA or a filter cutoff.
Fundamental/ADSR.try: Lengthen Attack to hear notes fade in. Set Sustain to 0 and shorten Decay for plucks.

params.Attack: Time to rise from 0 to 10 V after the gate starts. Short for percussive, long for pads.
params.Decay: Time to fall from the peak to the Sustain level while the gate is still held.
params.Sustain: The level held while the gate stays on, as a fraction of full. 0 gives a pluck no matter how long the key is held.
params.Release: Time to fall to 0 after the gate ends.
params.Push: A manual gate button: hold it to play the envelope by hand.

inputs.Gate: The note on/off signal. High starts the envelope, low releases it. From a sequencer gate, MIDI gate or clock.
inputs.Retrigger: A trigger here restarts the attack even while the gate is still held, for repeated notes without a gap.

outputs.Envelope: 0 to 10 V shape of the note. Into a VCA's CV for loudness, or a filter's Frequency input for tone.

Fundamental/VCMixer.about: A four channel mixer where every channel is also a VCA. Sum sources into one signal, set each level by knob or by CV.
Fundamental/VCMixer.try: Send two oscillators into Channel 1 and 2, the Mix out to the Audio module, and balance them.

params.Mix level: Overall output gain. 0 dB passes the sum unchanged.
params.Channel 1 level: Gain for channel 1; above 0 dB boosts.
params.Mix CV signal: How strongly the Mix CV input scales the mix level. 100 % means 10 V gives full level.
params.Channel 1 CV signal: How strongly the Channel 1 CV input scales channel 1.

inputs.Mix CV: CV that controls the whole mix level; an envelope here shapes the sum.
inputs.Channel 1 CV: CV for channel 1 level, so channel 1 works as a VCA.

outputs.Mix: All four channels summed, times Mix level.
outputs.Channel 1: Channel 1 alone, after its level and CV.

Fundamental/Scope.about: An oscilloscope: draws voltages over time so you can see what you hear. Its screen is only on the stock canvas for now; in this view it still passes signals through.

params.Gain 1: Vertical zoom for channel 1, volts per screen.
params.Offset 1: Shifts channel 1 up or down on screen.
params.Time: How many milliseconds one screen width shows. Short for waveforms, long for envelopes and LFOs.
params.Scope mode: 1 & 2 draws both channels against time. 1 x 2 plots channel 1 against channel 2 (a Lissajous figure).
params.Trigger threshold: The voltage channel 1 must cross to restart the trace, which keeps a repeating wave still on screen.
params.Trigger: Whether to wait for that crossing or just scroll.

inputs.External trigger: Restart the trace from a different signal, such as a clock.

Fundamental/SEQ3.about: An eight step sequencer with three rows of CV and a trigger per step. It walks along the steps on its own clock, sending the knob values of the current step. Row 1 to a VCO's pitch and the triggers to an envelope's gate make a melody.
Fundamental/SEQ3.try: Change Steps to 4 and the arpeggio becomes a four note loop. Turn a step's CV 1 knob while it plays to change that note.

params.Tempo: Speed of the internal clock, in beats per minute. Ignored when a Clock is patched in.
params.Run: Start and stop. The sequence holds its position while stopped.
params.Steps: How many steps play before looping: 1 to 8.

inputs.Tempo: CV that changes the internal tempo.
inputs.Clock: Advance one step per trigger from an external clock instead of the internal tempo. Lets several sequencers run in time.
inputs.Reset: A trigger jumps to step 1, for keeping it in step with other modules.
inputs.Steps: CV that changes the number of steps.

outputs.Trigger: A short pulse on every step whose trigger button is on. The usual gate source for the envelope.
outputs.CV 1: Row 1's value for the current step. Patch to a VCO Pitch jack for notes.
outputs.CV 2: Row 2's value: a second melody, or a filter sweep, or velocity.
outputs.Steps: The Steps setting as a voltage: number of steps minus one, so 8 steps gives 7 V. Patch it into another SEQ 3's Steps input to keep both the same length.
outputs.Clock: The clock, internal or passed through, for driving other modules.

Fundamental/SequentialSwitch1.about: One input, four outputs: each clock pulse sends the input to the next output in turn. Use it to spread one sequence across several destinations.

params.Steps: How many outputs to cycle through before returning to the first.

Fundamental/SequentialSwitch2.about: Four inputs, one output: each clock pulse picks the next input. Four different CVs clocked here make a four step sequence of whatever you patch in.

params.Steps: How many inputs to cycle through.

Fundamental/Quantizer.about: Rounds pitch CV to the nearest note of a scale, so a random or smoothly changing voltage plays in tune. The notes in the scale are chosen on the stock canvas for now.

params.Pre-offset: Shift the input by semitones before rounding, to transpose.

inputs.1V/octave pitch: Any CV you want turned into notes: an LFO, a random voltage, a sequencer row.

outputs.Pitch: The rounded pitch, 1 V per octave, ready for a VCO.

Fundamental/Split.about: Breaks a polyphonic cable (up to 16 voices in one wire) into separate mono outputs.

Fundamental/Merge.about: Combines up to 16 mono signals into one polyphonic cable.

outputs.Polyphonic: A polyphonic cable carrying every patched input as a voice.

Fundamental/Sum.about: Adds all voices of a polyphonic cable into one mono signal. The quick way to hear a polyphonic patch through a mono output.

Fundamental/MidSide.about: Converts stereo between left/right and mid/side, and back. Mid is what both channels share, side is what differs; widening or narrowing side changes the stereo width.

params.Encoder width: Scales the side signal when encoding: 0 % collapses to mono, 200 % exaggerates the stereo.
params.Decoder width: Scales side when decoding back to left/right.

Fundamental/Noise.about: Seven colours of noise, each with a different balance of low and high frequencies. Noise is the raw material for percussion, wind and breath, and for random voltages when sampled.

outputs.White noise: Equal energy at every frequency; hissy.
outputs.Pink noise: Equal energy per octave; sounds balanced, like rain.
outputs.Gray noise: Shaped to sound flat to the ear.
outputs.Black noise: Sparse, mostly silence with rare crackles.

Fundamental/Random.about: A random voltage generator with its own clock. Every clock tick it picks a new value, and gives it to you stepped, or smoothed in three different ways. The source of happy accidents in a patch.
Fundamental/Random.try: Patch Stepped into the Quantizer, the Quantizer into a VCO Pitch jack, and Trigger into an envelope Gate: a random melody in tune.

params.Clock rate: How often a new value is chosen, when no external Trigger is patched.
params.Shape: For the smoothed outputs, how the move from one value to the next is curved.
params.Offset: Bipolar (±5 V) or unipolar (0 to 10 V) output.
params.Trigger probability: Chance that a clock tick actually produces a new value. Below 100 % the pattern becomes irregular.
params.Random spread: How far a new value may land from the previous one. Low gives a wandering line, high gives jumps.
params.Clock rate CV: Depth of the Clock rate input.

inputs.Clock rate: CV for the internal clock speed.
inputs.Trigger: External clock: a new value on each trigger, replacing the internal clock.
inputs.External: Sample this voltage instead of generating a random one: turns the module into a sample and hold.

outputs.Stepped: Jumps straight to each new value and holds it.
outputs.Linear: Glides to each new value in a straight line.
outputs.Exponential: Glides fast at first then slows.
outputs.Trigger: A pulse whenever a new value is chosen; use it as the gate for the note it makes.

Cardinal/HostAudio2.about: The way out: whatever reaches the two inputs goes to the speaker or headphones, left and right. Every patch needs one of these. The outputs would carry sound from the host; in the browser there is no audio input, so they stay silent.

params.Level: Output volume in decibels. 0 dB is unchanged; keep the glyph's meter out of the white.

inputs.#0: Left speaker. Patch a mono signal here alone and you will only hear the left side; patch it to both for centre.

outputs.#0: Audio coming in from the host, left. Silent in the browser.
outputs.#1: Host audio in, right. Silent in the browser.

Cardinal/HostCV.about: Control voltages exchanged with a host DAW when Cardinal runs as a plugin. In the browser nothing is connected to the other side, so these jacks do nothing useful here.

params.Bipolar Inputs: Treat the host's inputs as ±5 V instead of 0 to 10 V.
params.Bipolar Outputs: Send ±5 V instead of 0 to 10 V.

Cardinal/HostMIDI.about: MIDI in and out. With a keyboard or controller connected (Android or desktop; iOS Safari has no Web MIDI), the outputs turn its notes into pitch and gate for the patch. The inputs send MIDI back out, which the browser build does not use.

outputs.1V/octave pitch: The last played note as pitch CV. Into a VCO's Pitch jack.
outputs.Gate: 10 V while a key is held. Into an envelope's Gate.
outputs.Velocity: How hard the key was hit, 0 to 10 V. Into a VCA CV or filter CV for expression.
outputs.Aftertouch: Pressure after the key is down, if the keyboard sends it.
outputs.Retrigger: A pulse on each new note, for restarting envelopes during legato.
outputs.Clock: MIDI clock pulses from the controller or DAW.
outputs.Clock divider: MIDI clock divided down, set on the module's panel.

inputs.1V/octave pitch: Pitch CV to send out as MIDI notes.

Cardinal/HostMIDICC.about: Sixteen MIDI continuous controllers (knobs and sliders on a controller) as CVs, 0 to 10 V, plus channel pressure and pitch bend. Which CC number each cell listens to is set on the module's own panel.

Cardinal/HostMIDIGate.about: Eighteen gates, one per chosen MIDI note: a drum pad controller becomes eighteen trigger sources. Note assignment is on the module's own panel.

Cardinal/HostMIDIMap.about: Maps incoming MIDI controllers directly onto knobs in the patch, without cables. Mapping is done on the stock canvas: pick a slot, move a knob, move the controller.

Cardinal/HostParameters.about: The 24 automatable parameters a host DAW exposes when Cardinal is a plugin, as CV outputs. In the browser there is no host, so they sit at 0 V.

Cardinal/HostParametersMap.about: Maps host plugin parameters onto knobs without cables. Needs a host DAW; nothing to do in the browser.

Cardinal/HostTime.about: Transport and tempo from the host, as gates and CVs. Standalone (including in the browser) Cardinal keeps its own transport, so the beat and bar pulses here can clock a patch even with no DAW.

outputs.#0: 10 V while the transport is playing.
outputs.#1: A pulse when the transport restarts.
outputs.#2: A pulse at the start of every bar.
outputs.#3: A pulse on every beat: a clock at the tempo.
outputs.#4: A faster pulse, several per beat (the division is set on the module's panel).
outputs.#5: Ramps 0 to 10 V across each bar.
outputs.#6: Ramps 0 to 10 V across each beat.
outputs.#7: Tempo as CV: log2 of BPM over 120, so 120 BPM is 0 V and 240 BPM is 1 V.

Cardinal/TextEditor.about: A notepad inside the patch. Nothing in the signal path; the startup patch uses it for its description. Editing happens on the stock canvas.

AriaSalvatrice/Spleet.about: Two polyphonic inputs, each split into four mono outputs. If only the first is patched, it splits into eight. Can sort voices by voltage so the lowest note is always on the first output.

params.Sort voltages on both banks: When on, the voices are reordered lowest to highest before being split.

inputs.Channel 1: Polyphonic bank 1 (or all eight voices when bank 2 is empty).

AriaSalvatrice/Swerge.about: Eight mono inputs merged into two polyphonic outputs of four voices each (or one of eight), with optional sorting by voltage.

params.Sort voltages on both banks: Reorder the merged voices lowest to highest.

AudibleInstruments/Plaits.about: A port of Mutable Instruments Plaits: sixteen synthesis engines in one oscillator, from virtual analogue and FM to strings, chords, speech and drums. Each engine reinterprets the same three knobs (Harmonics, Timbre, Morph), so learn one engine well and the others follow. It has a built-in lowpass gate, so a trigger alone can play a complete note.
AudibleInstruments/Plaits.try: Patch a sequencer Trigger into Trigger and its CV into Pitch, nothing on Level: Plaits plays plucked notes on its own. Then step through engines with the two model buttons.

params.Pitched models: Step to the next pitched engine (analogue waveforms, waveshaper, FM, grains, additive, wavetable, chords, speech).
params.Noise/percussive models: Step to the next noise or percussion engine (filtered noise, particles, string, modal, bass drum, snare, hi-hat).
params.Frequency: Coarse pitch, with the Pitch jack added at 1 V per octave.
params.Harmonics: Spectral content: for analogue engines the mix of waves, for FM the ratio, for chords the chord type. The knob to turn first in a new engine.
params.Timbre: The engine's main tone control: pulse width, wavefolding, FM index, string brightness and so on.
params.Morph: The engine's secondary dimension: morphs between variants, decay, structure.
params.Lowpass gate response: How the internal lowpass gate responds to a trigger: from a pure VCA (only loudness) to a VCF (loudness and brightness together, like a plucked string).
params.Lowpass gate decay: How long each triggered note rings.

inputs.Model: CV selects the engine, so a sequencer can switch sounds per step.
inputs.FM: Pitch modulation, through the Frequency CV knob.
inputs.Trigger: Starts a note through the internal lowpass gate. Patch this and you do not need an external envelope and VCA.
inputs.Level: 0 to 10 V opens the lowpass gate directly, like an external envelope; also controls the strike strength of percussive engines.

outputs.Auxiliary: A second flavour of the same engine: a sub oscillator, the raw excitation, a different mix. Often worth a listen.

Bogaudio/Bogaudio-VCO.about: Bogaudio's oscillator: four waveforms, a fine tune knob, built-in FM depth and a slow mode that turns it into an LFO.

params.Fine tune: Small pitch adjustment, within a semitone, for detuning against another oscillator.
params.Slow mode: Drops the whole range into LFO speeds.
params.FM depth: How much the FM input shifts the pitch.
params.FM mode: Exponential (in tune, musical) or linear (through-zero style timbres) FM.
params.Linear frequency: Makes the Frequency knob linear in Hz instead of in semitones, useful at LFO rates.

inputs.Sync: Restart the wave on each rising edge.

outputs.Square signal: Hollow, odd harmonics; pulse width applies.

Bogaudio/Bogaudio-LFO.about: Bogaudio's LFO: six shapes including a stepped random, with offset and scale knobs so the output lands exactly in the range the destination wants.

params.Frequency: Speed; the Pitch input adds to it at 1 V per octave.
params.Slow: Ten times slower overall, for minute-long sweeps.
params.Output sampling: Chops the smooth waves into steps; higher values give coarser, more stepped CV.
params.Offset: Shifts all outputs up or down in volts.
params.Scale: Attenuates all outputs; turn it down for subtle modulation.
params.Smoothing: Rounds the corners of the waves, including the stepped output.

inputs.Pitch (1V/octave): CV that changes the speed in octaves.

outputs.Stepped: A new random level each cycle, held.

Bogaudio/Bogaudio-VCF.about: A multimode filter: lowpass, highpass, bandpass or band reject from one output, with a variable slope. The Mode switch is what makes it different from Fundamental's VCF.

params.Center/cutoff frequency: Where the filter acts: the cutoff for low- and highpass, the centre for bandpass and band reject.
params.Frequency CV attenuation: Depth of the Cutoff CV input.
params.FM: Depth of the Cutoff FM input.
params.Resonance / bandwidth: Resonance at the cutoff, or the width of the band in bandpass modes.
params.Mode: Lowpass, highpass, bandpass or band reject (notch).
params.Slope: Steepness of the cut, in poles. Steeper removes more just past the cutoff.

inputs.Cutoff CV: CV for the cutoff, through its attenuator.
inputs.Cutoff FM: Fast modulation of the cutoff, through FM.
inputs.Cutoff pitch (1V/octave): Make the cutoff follow the note by patching the same pitch CV the oscillator gets.

Bogaudio/Bogaudio-AD.about: An attack/decay envelope: a trigger makes one rise and fall, with no sustain. Simpler than an ADSR and right for percussion; set it to loop and it is an LFO with adjustable shape.

params.Loop: Retrigger itself when the decay ends, turning it into a cycling LFO.
params.Retrigger: Allow a new trigger to restart the attack mid-envelope.

outputs.End-of-cycle trigger: A pulse when the decay finishes; chain to another AD or a sequencer.

Bogaudio/Bogaudio-RGate.about: A clock divider and multiplier with a gate length control. Feed it the master clock and get a slower or faster clock out with gates as long or short as you like.

params.Gate length: How long each output gate stays high, as a fraction of the period.
params.Clock division: Output one gate every N incoming clocks.
params.Clock multiplication: Output N gates per incoming clock.

inputs.Clock: The clock to divide or multiply.

Bogaudio/Bogaudio-Noise.about: Noise in five colours plus a utility that takes the absolute value of any signal.

inputs.Absolute value: Any signal; its negative half is flipped positive.

outputs.Gaussian noise: White noise with a bell-curve distribution.

Bogaudio/Bogaudio-SampleHold.about: Two sample-and-hold circuits. On each trigger the output grabs the input's voltage and holds it until the next trigger. Noise in, clock on trigger: a classic random stepped CV.

params.Track 1: Track and hold instead: follow the input while the gate is high, hold when low.

inputs.Signal 1: What to sample (noise if nothing is patched).

Bogaudio/Bogaudio-VCA.about: Two VCAs in 3 HP. Each has a level knob and a CV input that scales it.

params.Linear: Linear instead of exponential response to CV.

Bogaudio/Bogaudio-Switch81.about: Eight inputs to one output with a level knob per input. Use it as a mixer, or as a selector by leaving one knob up at a time; the panel's select CV picks inputs by voltage.

Bogaudio/Bogaudio-Switch18.about: One input to eight outputs, with a route knob per output. The mirror of SWITCH81: send one signal to several places, or to one of several places by CV.

Bogaudio/Bogaudio-AddrSeq.about: An eight step CV sequencer that can also be addressed directly: instead of stepping on a clock, a CV can choose which step's value appears. Eight knobs, one output.

params.Select step: Manually choose the step; the Select CV input adds to it.

inputs.Select CV: Choose a step by voltage; with no clock this makes it a CV-to-CV lookup table.

Bogaudio/Bogaudio-AddrSeqX.about: Expander for ADDR-SEQ: eight more steps. Must sit directly to the right of an ADDR-SEQ on the stock canvas to do anything.

Bogaudio/Bogaudio-Unison.about: Turns one pitch and gate into a polyphonic cable of several detuned copies, for thick unison sounds from a polyphonic oscillator.

params.Detune: How far apart the voices are spread in pitch.

inputs.Gate: The gate to copy to every voice.

outputs.Pitch (1V/octave): Polyphonic pitch, one detuned copy per voice.

Bogaudio/Bogaudio-Offset.about: Adds a voltage to a signal and scales it. The tool for getting a CV into the range a destination wants, or for making a constant voltage with nothing patched in.

params.Scale: Multiplier applied after the offset; negative inverts.

inputs.Signal: The signal to shift; leave empty to output a steady voltage.

Bogaudio/Bogaudio-Slew.about: A slew limiter: it refuses to let a voltage change faster than a set rate, separately for rising and falling. On a pitch CV it is portamento; on a gate it becomes a simple envelope.
Bogaudio/Bogaudio-Slew.try: Patch the sequencer's CV 1 through Slew before the VCO Pitch jack and raise Rise and Fall: the notes glide into each other.

params.Rise: How long an upward step takes.
params.Rise shape: Curve of the rise, from logarithmic through linear to exponential.
params.Fall: How long a downward step takes.

Bogaudio/Bogaudio-Switch.about: A two channel A/B switch controlled by a gate. Each channel passes its High input while the gate is on and its Low input while it is off.

params.Latch: Each gate pulse toggles the switch instead of following the gate level.

inputs.High 1 signal: Channel 1 when the gate is high.
inputs.Low 1 signal: Channel 1 when the gate is low.
inputs.Hight 2 signal: Channel 2 when the gate is high.
inputs.Low 2 signal: Channel 2 when the gate is low.

ImpromptuModular/Clocked.about: A master clock with three derived clocks, each at its own ratio of the master, with swing, pulse width and delay per clock. The heart of a rhythm patch: one tempo, several related pulses.
ImpromptuModular/Clocked.try: Set Clk 1 ratio to 1, Clk 2 to 1/2 and Clk 3 to 4, then patch each to a different envelope: a kick, a half-time hat and a sixteenth note shaker from one tempo.

params.Clk 1 ratio: Clock 1 as a multiple or division of the master.
params.Swing clk: Delay every other master pulse for a shuffle feel.
params.Pulse width clk: How long the master gate stays high.
params.Delay clk 1: Shift clock 1 later by a fraction of a beat.
params.Bpm mode prev: Step the external clock mode back (how the BPM CV input is interpreted).
params.Bpm mode next: Step the external clock mode forward.

inputs.BPM CV / Ext clock: Set the tempo by CV, or follow an external clock, depending on the BPM mode.

outputs.Reset: Reset pulse, to pass on to sequencers.
outputs.BPM CV / Ext clock thru: The BPM input passed through, for chaining.

ImpromptuModular/Clocked-Expander.about: Expander for Clocked: CV control over each clock's pulse width and swing. Must sit directly right of Clocked on the stock canvas.

ImpromptuModular/Clocked-Clkd.about: The compact Clocked: master tempo and three ratio clocks, without swing, pulse width or delay.

ImpromptuModular/Gate-Seq-64.about: A 64 step gate sequencer for rhythm: four tracks of up to 16 steps (or fewer tracks with more steps), each step a gate on or off with a choice of gate pattern and probability. Drive it from Clocked and patch each track to a drum voice's trigger.

params.Length / run mode: Set the sequence length, or the run direction.
params.Configuration: How the 64 buttons are divided: 4 tracks × 16, 2 × 32 or 1 × 64.
params.Probability: Chance a step's gate fires, for the selected step.
params.Seq/song mode: Edit one sequence, or chain sequences into a song.
params.Sequence: Which of the stored sequences is shown.

ImpromptuModular/Gate-Seq-64-Expander.about: Expander for GateSeq64: CV inputs for writing steps and probability. Must sit directly right of GateSeq64 on the stock canvas.

MockbaModular/Filtah.about: A tiny filter: lowpass, highpass or bandpass with cutoff, resonance and output gain.

params.#1: Cutoff, as a percentage of the range.

MockbaModular/Mixah.about: A two input crossfader with a VCA: blend A and B by knob or CV, then scale the result.

params.#0: 0 is all A, 1 is all B.
params.B Phase: Invert B before mixing, so equal signals cancel.

inputs.#1: CV that scales the output, like a VCA.

MockbaModular/Pannah.about: A panner: one signal placed between left and right by knob or CV.

inputs.#0: CV for the position; an LFO here is auto-pan.

MockbaModular/ReVoltah.about: A voltage rescaler: maps an input range onto an output range. For example ±5 V in to 0 to 10 V out, or inverting by swapping the output min and max.

MockbaModular/CZOsc.about: An oscillator modelled on Casio's phase distortion synths: eight waveforms whose Shape knob bends a sine into brighter forms, like a filter sweep without a filter.

params.#0: One of eight phase distortion waveforms.
params.#1: Run at LFO speeds instead of audio.
params.Fine frequency / LFO Offset: Fine tune (or offset when in LFO mode).
params.Shape: Amount of distortion: 0 is a sine, up is brighter.

inputs.#1: CV for Shape; an envelope here gives the classic CZ sweep.

MockbaModular/MaugOsc.about: An oscillator with Moog-style waveforms (triangle, saw, shark tooth, pulses) in 2 HP.

params.Fine frequency / LFO Offset: Fine tune, or offset in LFO mode.

SurgeXTRack/SurgeXTWaveshaper.about: Surge's waveshaper: dozens of distortion curves from soft saturation to folding and digital mangling, with drive, bias and filters either side. Stereo in and out.

params.Drive: How hard the signal hits the curve.
params.Bias: Shifts the signal before shaping, making the distortion asymmetric.

SurgeXTRack/SurgeXTOSCModern.about: Surge's Modern oscillator: a mixable saw, pulse and triangle with sync, sub oscillator and up to 16 unison voices. One module can sound like a whole analogue polysynth's oscillator section.

params.Pitch (v/oct): Pitch offset added to the V/Oct input.
params.Sync: Hard sync amount against an internal master.
params.Random Phase on Retrigger: Start each note at a random phase.
params.Absolute Unison: Detune in Hz rather than cents.

outputs.Left (or Mono merged): Left, or everything when Right is unpatched.

SurgeXTRack/SurgeXTOSCSine.about: Surge's Sine oscillator: a sine with 27 shaping variants, feedback FM on itself and unison. Clean sub tones at one end, harsh FM at the other.

params.Feedback: Self FM amount; the main tone control.

outputs.Left (or Mono merged): Left, or everything when Right is unpatched.

SurgeXTRack/SurgeXTFXNimbus.about: Surge's port of the Mutable Instruments Clouds granular processor. It records the incoming sound into a buffer and replays it as grains: tiny slices whose position, size, pitch and density you control. Freeze the buffer and a chord becomes a cloud. Stereo.
SurgeXTRack/SurgeXTFXNimbus.try: Send the VCA output through Nimbus to Audio, raise Mix to full and Density to the middle, then tap Manual Freeze while the arpeggio plays.

params.Mode: Granular, pitch shifter/time stretch, looping delay or spectral madness.
params.Quality: Buffer sample rate and stereo/mono; lower quality means a longer buffer.
params.Position: Where in the buffer grains are taken from: now, or seconds ago.
params.Pitch: Transposition of the grains, in semitones.
params.Density: How often grains fire; centre is sparse, outwards is dense, one side random the other regular.
params.Texture: Grain envelope shape, from clicky to smooth, into diffusion.
params.Freeze: Stop recording; the buffer loops as it is.
params.Feedback: Feed output back into the buffer.

inputs.Left Sideband: Extra left input mixed into the buffer.

outputs.Left (or Mono merged): Left, or everything when Right is unpatched.

SurgeXTRack/SurgeXTLFO.about: Surge's LFO and envelope combined: a waveform (sine, triangle, square, ramps, noise, sample and hold, a 16 step sequencer) multiplied by a DAHDSR envelope, with tempo sync. Three outputs give the product, the wave alone or the envelope alone.

params.Release: Envelope fade after the gate ends.

inputs.Gate for Full LFO (env + wave): Gate that restarts the LFO and runs the envelope.
inputs.Gate for Envelope Only: Gate for the envelope while the wave free-runs.
inputs.Direct Phase (0-10v for 0-1 Phase): Drive the phase directly with a CV.

outputs.Trigger on end of Envelope Stage or Step: Pulse at envelope stage ends, or step trigger A.
outputs.Trigger on end of Envelope or Step Trigg: Pulse at envelope end, or step trigger B.

SurgeXTRack/SurgeXTMixer.about: Surge's oscillator mixer: three stereo inputs plus a noise source and two ring modulators (1×2, 2×3), each with level, mute and solo.

params.RingMod 1X2 Level: Level of input 1 multiplied by input 2: metallic sum and difference tones.
params.Noise Color: Tilt of the noise from dark to bright.

SurgeXTRack/SurgeXTMixerSlider.about: The same Surge mixer with sliders instead of knobs: three stereo inputs, noise, two ring modulators, mute and solo per source.

SurgeXTRack/SurgeXTModMatrix.about: A modulation matrix: four modulator inputs, eight target outputs, and a depth knob for every pairing. Set a base value per target and add any mix of the modulators to it. Saves a rack full of attenuators and offsets.
